major.name: Japanese Studies - BA

requirement.label: Japanese language
requirement.notes: two years of lower-division courses or the transferred equivalent from JAPN 10A-B-C, JAPN 20A-B-C. The language requirement may be waived by demonstrating the equivalent proficiency through exam.

items.label: Japanese language: six upper-division language courses
items.notes: six upper-division language courses or the transferred equivalent. The language requirement can be waived by demonstrating the equivalent proficiency through exam; the required number of courses must then be fulfilled by taking other upper-division nonlanguage courses. Students may petition to include upper-division language courses taken abroad under the Education Abroad Program (EAP) or Opportunities Abroad Program (OAP).

items.text: Students may petition to include upper-division nonlanguage courses taken abroad under EAP or OAP.

items.label: The remaining five courses
items.notes: The remaining five courses must be taken from two or more different disciplines, from the list of upper-division courses applicable for the major. Students may include one 199 (Special Studies) course. JAPN 135A-C, 137A-C and 150A-C appear on that list (under Japanese Studies) and are kept here.

narrative: All upper-division courses must be taken for a letter grade, with the exception of JAPN 199.
Students who declare for the Japanese studies major and minor will be allowed no more than one course with a D grade to count toward the program requirements.
The language requirement can be waived by demonstrating the equivalent proficiency through exam. The required number of courses must be fulfilled by taking other upper-division nonlanguage courses.

All graduate-level courses require consent of the instructor/department for undergraduate students. Courses marked with an asterisk (*) in the catalog (e.g., COMM 113, HIEA 144, HIEA 150, HIEA 180, LTWL 155, LTCS courses, MUS 111, MUS 116, TDGE 126, VIS 128E) may require departmental approval via student petition; approval is given only when content relates primarily to Japan.
Lower-division requirement is headed "(nine courses)"; the courses listed are JAPN 10A-B-C and JAPN 20A-B-C.
The degree (BA) is not stated on the catalog page.

groups: B. Upper-Division Requirement (twelve courses): The remaining five courses

nodes.description: Explores films from China, India, Japan and other Asian countries. Popular, documentary, and ethnographic films are examined for what they reveal about family life, gender, politics, religion, social change and everyday experience in South Asia.

nodes.title: Japan: Twelfth- to Mid-Nineteenth Centuries
groups: B. Upper-Division Requirement (twelve courses): The remaining five courses
nodes.description: Covers important political issues—such as the medieval decentralization of state power, unification in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries, the Tokugawa system of rule, and conflicts between rulers and ruled—while examining long-term changes in economy, society, and culture. +

nodes.title: Japan: From the Mid-Nineteenth Century through the US Occupation
groups: B. Upper-Division Requirement (twelve courses): The remaining five courses
nodes.description: Topics include the Meiji Restoration, nationalism, industrialization, imperialism, Taisho Democracy, and the Occupation. Special attention will be given to the costs as well as benefits of “modernization” and the relations between dominant and subordinated cultures and groups within Japan.

nodes.title: The Fifteen-Year War in Asia and the Pacific
groups: B. Upper-Division Requirement (twelve courses): The remaining five courses
nodes.description: Lecture-discussion course approaching the 1931–1945 war through various “local,” rather than simply national, experiences. Perspectives examined include those of marginalized groups within Japan, Japanese Americans, Pacific Islanders, and other elites and nonelites in Asian and Pacific settings.

nodes.title: Postwar Japan
groups: B. Upper-Division Requirement (twelve courses): The remaining five courses
nodes.description: Examines social, cultural, political, and economic transformations and continuities in Japan since World War II. Emphases will differ by instructor.

nodes.title: Social and Cultural History of Twentieth-Century Japan
groups: B. Upper-Division Requirement (twelve courses): The remaining five courses
nodes.description: Japanese culture and society changed dramatically during the twentieth century. This course will focus on the transformation of cultural codes into what we know as “Japanese,” the politics of culture, and the interaction between individuals and society.

nodes.title: Japan-U.S. Relations
groups: B. Upper-Division Requirement (twelve courses): The remaining five courses
nodes.description: Survey of relations between Japan and the United States in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries. Although the focus will be on these nation-states, the course will be framed within the global transformation of societies. Topics include cultural frameworks, political and economic changes, colonialism and imperialism, and migration.

nodes.title: Ghosts in Japan
groups: B. Upper-Division Requirement (twelve courses): The remaining five courses
nodes.description: By examining the roles of ghosts in Japanese belief systems in a nonscientific age, this course addresses topics including folk beliefs and ghost stories, religiosity, early science, tools of amelioration and authoritative knowledge, and the relationship between myth and history.

groups: B. Upper-Division Requirement (twelve courses): The remaining five courses

nodes.title: Women and Gender in East Asia
groups: B. Upper-Division Requirement (twelve courses): The remaining five courses
nodes.description: The impact of modern transformations on female roles and gender relations in China, Japan, and Korea, focusing on the late imperial/early modern periods through the twentieth century.

nodes.title: Topics in East Asian History
groups: B. Upper-Division Requirement (twelve courses): The remaining five courses
nodes.description: Selected topics in East Asian History. Course may be taken for credit up to three times as topics vary.

nodes.title: Modern Korea, 1800–1945
groups: B. Upper-Division Requirement (twelve courses): The remaining five courses
nodes.description: This course examines Korea’s entrance into the modern world. It utilizes both textual and audio-visual materials to explore local engagements with global phenomenon, such as imperialism, nationalism, capitalism, and socialism. HILD 10, 11, and/or 12 recommended.

groups: B. Upper-Division Requirement (twelve courses): The remaining five courses

nodes.description: This colloquium will examine selected topics in modern Korean history through both primary sources (in translation) and secondary sources. Topics will vary year to year.

groups: B. Upper-Division Requirement (twelve courses)
nodes.description: This course focuses on interdisciplinary approaches to the study of Japan ranging across disciplines and emphasizing modern Japan in both domestic and transnational contexts. The course is conducted as a seminar and combines analysis and discussion of readings with instruction and experience in conducting original research, writing academic research papers, and presentation of student work to the class.

groups: B. Upper-Division Requirement (twelve courses): The remaining five courses
nodes.description: A reading of recent theory on popular culture and a study of particular texts dealing with popular cultural practices, both contemporary and noncontemporary, as sites of conflict and struggle. LTCS 110 and LTCS 110GS may be taken for credit for a combined total of three times.

nodes.title: Historical Perspectives on Culture
groups: B. Upper-Division Requirement (twelve courses): The remaining five courses
nodes.description: The course will explore the relation among cultural production, institutions, history, and ideology during selected historical periods. In considering different kinds of texts, relations of power and knowledge at different historical moments will be discussed. May be taken for credit up to three times as topics vary.

nodes.title: Cultural Perspectives on Immigration and Citizenship
groups: B. Upper-Division Requirement (twelve courses): The remaining five courses
nodes.description: Introduction to the studies of cultural dimensions of immigration and citizenship. Examines the diverse cultural texts—literature, law, film, music, the televisual images, etc.—that both shape and are shaped by immigration and the idea of citizenship in different national and historical contexts. May be taken for credit up to two times as topics vary.

nodes.title: Gender, Race/Ethnicity, Class, and Culture
groups: B. Upper-Division Requirement (twelve courses): The remaining five courses
nodes.description: The course will focus on the representation of gender, ethnicity, and class in cultural production in view of various contemporary theories of race, sex, and class. May be taken for credit up to three times as topics vary.

nodes.title: Topics in Queer Cultures/Queer Subcultures
groups: B. Upper-Division Requirement (twelve courses): The remaining five courses
nodes.description: This course examines the intersection of sex, sexuality, and popular culture by looking at the history of popular representations of queer sexuality and their relation to political movements for gay and lesbian rights. May be taken for credit up to three times as topics vary.

nodes.title: Special Topics in Social Identities and the Media
groups: B. Upper-Division Requirement (twelve courses): The remaining five courses
nodes.description: A study of media representation and various aspects of identity, such as gender, sexuality, race, ethnicity, social class, culture, and geopolitical location. Students will consider the various media of film, television, alternative video, advertising, music, and the internet. May be taken for credit up to three times as topics vary.

nodes.title: Globalization and Culture
groups: B. Upper-Division Requirement (twelve courses): The remaining five courses
nodes.description: Studies of cultural dimensions of immigration and citizenship. This course examines the diverse cultural texts—literature, law, film, music, the televisual images, etc., that both shape and are shaped by immigration and the idea of citizenship in different national and historical contexts. May be taken for credit up to two times as topics vary.

nodes.title: Special Topics in Race and Empire
groups: B. Upper-Division Requirement (twelve courses): The remaining five courses
nodes.description: The role of race and culture within the history of empires; may select a single empire for consideration, such as France, Britain, United States, or Japan, or choose to examine the role of race and culture in comparative histories of colonialism. May be taken for credit up to three times as topics vary.

nodes.title: Topics in Cultural Studies
groups: B. Upper-Division Requirement (twelve courses): The remaining five courses
nodes.description: The course will examine one or more forms of cultural production or cultural practice from a variety of theoretical and historical perspectives. Topics may include contemporary debates on culture, genres of popular music/fiction/film, AIDS and culture, the history of sexuality, subcultural styles, etc. May be taken for credit up to three times as topics vary.

nodes.title: Visual Culture

nodes.description: The course will focus on visual practices and discourses in their intersection and overlap, from traditional media, print, and photography to film, video, TV, computers, medical scanners, and the internet. May be taken for credit up to three times as topics vary.

nodes.title: Later Japanese Literature in Translation

nodes.description: An introduction to later Japanese (kogo) literature in translation. Will focus on several “modern” works, placing their forms in the historical context. No knowledge of Japanese required. May be taken for credit up to three times as topics vary.

nodes.title: Gender Studies

nodes.description: This course examines special topics in popular music from various sociopolitical, aesthetic, and performance perspectives. Readings include recent literature in cultural studies, musicology, and/or performance practice. Topics vary. May be taken for credit three times.

nodes.title: Chinese and Japanese Political Thought I
groups: B. Upper-Division Requirement (twelve courses): The remaining five courses
nodes.prereq_text: upper-division standing for POLI 113B.
nodes.description: Examines philosophical traditions of ancient and modern China and Japan, to understand how these have been reflected in Chinese and Japanese development. Course will be in English; however, students with Chinese or Japanese language skills will have the opportunity to use these. Graduate students will be required to complete a seminar-length research paper; undergraduate students will write a paper.

nodes.title: Chinese and Japanese Political Thought I

nodes.prereq_text: upper-division standing for POLI 113B.
nodes.description: Examines philosophical traditions of ancient and modern China and Japan, to understand how these have been reflected in Chinese and Japanese development. Course will be in English; however, students with Chinese or Japanese language skills will have the opportunity to use these. Graduate students will be required to complete a seminar-length research paper; undergraduate students will write a paper.

nodes.title: Chinese and Japanese Political Thought II
groups: B. Upper-Division Requirement (twelve courses): The remaining five courses
nodes.prereq_text: POLI 113B or 113BR.
nodes.description: A continuation of 113B, which follows political philosophical themes in China and Japan through the twentieth century. Important topics include Buddhism and Confucianism as they changed in each context in response to internal and external stimuli.

groups: B. Upper-Division Requirement (twelve courses): The remaining five courses

nodes.title: Japanese Politics: A Developmental Perspective
groups: B. Upper-Division Requirement (twelve courses): The remaining five courses
nodes.description: This course will analyze the political systems of modern Japan in comparative-historical perspective.

nodes.title: Political Institutions of East Asian Countries
groups: B. Upper-Division Requirement (twelve courses): The remaining five courses
nodes.description: This course discusses the following major topics in three East Asian countries (Japan, South Korea, and the Philippines) from a comparative perspective: (a) economic and political development; (b) political institutions; and (c) policies.

groups: B. Upper-Division Requirement (twelve courses): The remaining five courses

nodes.title: Postwar US-Japan Relations
groups: B. Upper-Division Requirement (twelve courses): The remaining five courses
nodes.description: The relationship between the United States and Japan has been described as “the most important in the world, bar none.” This course will examine US-Japan security and economic relations in the postwar period from the Occupation and Cold War alliance through the severe bilateral trade friction of the 1980s and 1990s to the present relationship and how it is being transformed by the forces of globalization, regionalization, and multilateralism.

nodes.title: Japanese Culture Inside/Out: A Transnational Perspective
groups: B. Upper-Division Requirement (twelve courses): The remaining five courses
nodes.prereq_text: upper-division standing.
nodes.description: We examine cultural production in Japan and abroad, national and transnational political-economic and social influences, the idea of Japan in the West, and the idea of the West in Japan.

groups: B. Upper-Division Requirement (twelve courses): The remaining five courses

nodes.title: Storytelling and Design in Animation
groups: B. Upper-Division Requirement (twelve courses): The remaining five courses
nodes.prereq_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor.
nodes.description: This course will use a broad range of animation styles and genres to examine larger issues in art practice, focusing closely on the relationship between form and content, and how sound/set/costume/character design impacts narrative.

nodes.title: Twentieth-Century Art in China and Japan
groups: B. Upper-Division Requirement (twelve courses): The remaining five courses
nodes.prereq_text: upper-division standing.
nodes.description: Surveys the key works and developments in the modern art and visual culture of Japan from Edo and Meiji to the present and of China from the early-twentieth century to contemporary video, performance, and installation art. Recommended preparation: VIS 21B.

nodes.title: Arts of Japan
groups: B. Upper-Division Requirement (twelve courses): The remaining five courses
nodes.prereq_text: upper-division standing.
nodes.description: Course is a survey of the visual arts of Japan, considering how the arts developed in the context of Japan’s history and discussing how art and architecture were used for philosophical, religious, and material ends. Recommended preparation: VIS 21B.

nodes.title: Topics in Art History and Theory
groups: B. Upper-Division Requirement (twelve courses): The remaining five courses
nodes.prereq_text: none.
nodes.description: These lecture courses are on topics of special interest to visiting and permanent faculty. Topics vary from term to term and with instructor and many will not be repeated. These courses fulfill upper-division distribution requirements. As the courses under this heading will be offered less frequently than those of the regular curriculum, students are urged to check with the visual arts department academic advising office for availability and descriptions of these supplementary courses. Like the courses listed under VIS 129, below, the letters following the course number designate the general area in which the courses fall. Students may take courses with the same number but of different content, for a total of three times for credit. Recommended preparation: courses in art history (VIS 113AN–129F).
